resolutions.title: Site 2's ownership pointer is false for the archive half of the override's own domain
resolutions.action: RATIFIED IN CHAT: option (A) — name BOTH owners. Verified in full before acting, and all four claims hold: orbit-run-summary-emit's Purpose enumerates the WORKFLOW commands and then says 'alongside the existing editorial and lifecycle emit-producing commands', so archive is explicitly elsewhere; its gate_overridden table entry and scenario both sit inside `Apply per-chunk-end emission` naming apply-<TS>.json and review-proposal; orbit-archive-modifications:111 states {gate, state, reason} for the archive; and the edited requirement's FIRST scenario is `Override recorded, not prevented` — 'the user proceeds past an unpassed review-system gate at archive'. So the single-owner pointer sent a reader to the wrong capability for the requirement's own opening scenario. The clause now reads: the record's SHAPE is owned by the EMITTING COMMAND'S OWN CAPABILITY — orbit-run-summary-emit for the apply emit, orbit-archive-modifications for the archive emit — mirroring the precedent at orbit-run-summary-emit:567 (the consent field), one requirement away in the file the pointer targets. Option (B), retreating to a plain substitution, was briefed and rejected: it would forfeit the reason the ownership move was ratified, which was to stop rc04c returning to a capability this stage had finished with. CASCADED to all three other in-set sites (design.md D2, explore.md's D-rc04d-2 table row, tasks.md 1.2), each carrying the correction AS a correction rather than silently — the row now records what the original said and why it was wrong, because the error propagated through four artifacts by faithful transcription and the next reader should see that happen.

resolutions.title: De-naming 4a widens `orbit-pr-lifecycle`'s READY rule across two distinct archive-seam overrides
resolutions.action: Qualified the noun: 'a recorded proceed-anyway override AT THE `review-system` GATE SHALL still flip READY'. Verified the finding's premise first — orbit-archive-modifications:116 does spend a sentence keeping the two archive-seam overrides apart ('This is distinct from `gate_overridden` (review-cadence override)'), so the unqualified substitution really did extend a normative SHALL, and its trailing justification clause ('the recorded override IS the user's ratification'), across a content-guard override nobody argued it for. Behaviour is unaffected either way, which is why this is precision loss rather than a false claim — but it is precisely the risk this change's own register names, and the D-rc04d-2 table did not catch it. The scenario needed no change: it is already anchored by 'the gate inflection prompt's Proceed-anyway'.

final_assessment: The fresh proposal pass walked to zero: 7 findings, 1 CRITICAL, all resolved, none stale, none deferred. The CRITICAL is the one that matters and it was correct — this stage's single substantive edit named the wrong capability as owner of the override record's shape for the ARCHIVE half of the requirement's domain, and the requirement's own opening scenario is that half. Ratified option A: name both owners, mirroring a precedent sitting one requirement away in the very file the pointer targets. The reviewer's diagnosis is worth more than the fix — the error was authored in a sibling exploration's table and then transcribed faithfully into explore, proposal, design and delta, so the transcribe-don't-re-derive discipline that protected the four easy substitutions is exactly what carried the one unverified claim through four artifacts unexamined. That is a real limit on a practice this session has been treating as pure upside. Two findings were my own residue from earlier in the same session: rc04c's Touches slot, where the architect session rewrote the scope paragraph and left the machine-shaped line, and the exit-criteria softness in a stage whose design argues exit criteria should be mechanisms. Post-walk: 27 scenarios intact, 0 set mismatches, fingerprints 5/5, 2238 tests green, validate --strict clean.
